data.long_meaning: Mahadev is a popular name for Lord Shiva, the supreme God in Hinduism. The name Mahadev carries the meaning “Great God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mahadev usually hope their child will grow to embody great god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Mahadev belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Great God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mahadev total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Mahadev" holds great cultural significance in Hinduism. It is a revered title for Lord Shiva, who is considered the god of destruction and the families, who have a family deity named Lord Shiva, often call Lord Shiva as "Mahadev". Mahadev is also known as the 'Pramathman', the greatest among all beings. The name also signifies divine power and authority, strength, and fearlessness. The image of Mahadev, with the third eye, snake around his neck, and a crescent moon on his forehead, is a transcendent and powerful representation of divinity in Hindu culture. Mahadev is also a common name for temples dedicated to Lord Shiva.
data.spiritual_significance: Mahadev, as Lord Shiva, signifies the ultimate reality, the ultimate truth of the universe. He represents the eternal, unchanging consciousness that lies at the core of creation. Mahadev is the destroyer of both negative emotions and negative physical entities, paving the way for creation and new beginnings. He represents the transcendental aspect of God, being beyond the dualities of creation and destruction. He is the embodiment of eternal bliss and salvation, and devotion to Mahadev is believed to lead towards self-realization and spiritual growth. According to some Hindu texts, the sound of the name Mahadev is believed to invoke Lord Shiva, and merely uttering the name is considered a powerful spiritual practice.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Mahadev, meaning 'Great God', symbolizes the supreme cosmic power and reverence towards the ultimate reality. It is a name that embodies the essence of Shiva as the creator, destroyer, and preserver of the universe.

vedic_reference.note: An epithet of Lord Shiva, not a direct Vedic reference

historical_references.reference: Shiva is referred to as Mahadeva in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic. The name Mahadeva means 'The Great God'. The epic describes Shiva as the supreme deity, responsible for the creation and destruction of the universe.

The name Mahadeva is also associated with Shiva in the Puranas, a set of Indian scriptures. Mahadeva is considered an aspect of Shiva, representing his supreme power and greatness. The Puranas describe various tales and legends surrounding Mahadeva and his roles in creation and destruction.

modern_usage.modern_context: Mahadev, also known as Lord Shiva, is a significant deity in Hinduism. In modern times, Mahadev is often depicted in various forms and contexts that reflect his role as the destroyer of evil and the god of regeneration and transformation. On Instagram, Mahadev is a popular hashtag (#Mahadev) for spiritual and inspirational content, including images of Shiva idols, temples, and natural landscapes. On Reddit, there is a subreddit (r/Mahadev) dedicated to discussing various aspects of Lord Shiva and his symbolism. On Quora, there are numerous questions related to Mahadev and Hinduism, such as 'Who is Lord Mahadev?' and 'What are the symbols of Lord Mahadev?'.
